scenes.animation: Zippy spreads out a map of South India and lays a ruler between Bengaluru and Chennai. It reads '5 cm'. He cheers, 'Chennai is only 5 cm away! I'll walk!'

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: Chennai is just 5 centimetres from Bengaluru. I'll walk there before lunch!

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Look at the corner of the map first. There's a ratio hiding there.

scenes.animation: The map corner zooms in: 'RF 1 : 60,00,000'. A label: 'Representative Fraction = map distance : actual distance'. A 1 cm segment stretches out across the landscape to a signpost '60,00,000 cm'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: This is the Representative Fraction, or RF. It is the ratio of a distance on the map to the actual distance on the ground.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: 1 is to 60 lakh means 1 centimetre on the map stands for 60 lakh centimetres on the ground.

scenes.animation: Conversion steps line by line: '100 cm = 1 m', '1000 m = 1 km', '1 km = 1,00,000 cm', '60,00,000 cm ÷ 1,00,000 = 60 km'. Then '5 cm × 60 km = 300 km'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: A kilometre is 1000 metres, and each metre is 100 centimetres. So 1 kilometre is 1 lakh centimetres.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: 60 lakh centimetres divided by 1 lakh is 60 kilometres. So 1 centimetre on this map means 60 kilometres.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Your 5 centimetres is 5 times 60, which is about 300 kilometres.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: Three hundred kilometres! That's a lot more than a morning walk.

scenes.animation: A dotted straight line joins the two cities 'as the crow flies', while a winding road snakes between them. Labels: 'geographical distance' on the straight line and 'road distance' on the road. An 'Exam Tip' sticker: 'Convert cm to km: divide by 1,00,000'.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: So the bus will travel exactly 300 kilometres?

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Not quite. The map gives straight-line, geographical distance. Roads bend, so road distance is usually more.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Exam tip: when using an RF, convert centimetres to kilometres by dividing by 1 lakh.

scenes.animation: Students sketch their classroom on graph paper with the scale '1 : 50'. The teacher's desk, blackboard, fans and lights appear as small symbols. A 6 m wall becomes '600 cm ÷ 50 = 12 cm' on paper.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Try making your own map. Draw your classroom at 1 is to 50.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: A wall 6 metres long is 600 centimetres. Divided by 50, that's 12 centimetres on your paper.

scenes.animation: Recap board over the South India map. Points: '1. RF = map distance : actual distance', '2. 1 : 60,00,000 → 1 cm = 60 km', '3. Maps show straight-line, not road, distance'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Recap.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: One: the Representative Fraction compares map distance to actual distance.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Two: at 1 is to 60 lakh, 1 centimetre on the map is 60 kilometres.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Three: maps give straight-line distance, which is usually shorter than road distance.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: Okay. I'll take the bus.

name: Ratios with More Than Two Terms

scenes.animation: Viswanath grinds a spice mix in a mixer: '8 spoons coriander : 4 red chillies : 2 spoons toor dal : 1 spoon methi'. Puneet opens his kitchen shelf and finds only 2 red chillies.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: Puneet wants the same spice mix, but he has only 2 red chillies.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: This ratio has four terms: 8 is to 4 is to 2 is to 1. Every term must change by the same factor.

scenes.animation: The ratio '8 : 4 : 2 : 1' gets '× 1/2' arrows on every term, giving '4 : 2 : 1 : 0.5'. The two ratios are joined by '::'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Puneet has half the chillies, so he halves everything.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: 4 spoons of coriander, 2 chillies, 1 spoon of toor dal and half a spoon of methi. That's 4 is to 2 is to 1 is to 0.5.

scenes.animation: Paint tins: 'Red : Blue : White = 2 : 3 : 5'. Yasmin has 10 L of white. Steps: '5 parts = 10 L', '1 part = 2 L', 'red = 4 L, blue = 6 L', 'total = 20 L'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Yasmin mixes purple paint in the ratio red to blue to white of 2 is to 3 is to 5. She has 10 litres of white.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: White is 5 parts, so 1 part is 2 litres. Red is 4 litres and blue is 6 litres, making 20 litres of purple.

scenes.animation: A construction site with concrete ratio 'cement : sand : gravel = 1 : 1.5 : 3'. Steps build: '1 + 1.5 + 3 = 5.5', '110 ÷ 5.5 = 20', 'cement 20, sand 30, gravel 60', 'check: 20 + 30 + 60 = 110 ✓'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Strong concrete for pillars uses cement, sand and gravel in the ratio 1 is to 1.5 is to 3. We need 110 units.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: One batch is 1 plus 1.5 plus 3, which is 5.5 units. 110 divided by 5.5 is 20 batches.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: So 20 units of cement, 30 of sand and 60 of gravel. Check: 20 plus 30 plus 60 is 110.

scenes.animation: Puzzle card: 'Triangle angles in ratio 1 : 3 : 5'. Steps: '1 + 3 + 5 = 9', '180 ÷ 9 = 20', 'angles 20°, 60°, 100°'. A protractor draws the triangle. An 'Exam Tip' sticker: 'Divide the whole by the SUM of the terms'.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: Puzzle for you: a triangle's angles are in the ratio 1 is to 3 is to 5.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: The angles add to 180. The terms add to 9, and 180 divided by 9 is 20.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: So the angles are 20, 60 and 100 degrees.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Exam tip: to split a whole in a ratio, divide by the sum of all the terms, then multiply by each term.

scenes.animation: Recap board with the spice jar, paint tins and triangle. Points: '1. Ratios can have many terms', '2. Scale every term by the same factor', '3. Share x in a : b : c → x × a/(a + b + c), ...'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Recap.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: One: ratios can have three, four or more terms.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Two: to keep the mix the same, scale every term by the same factor.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Three: to share a whole, divide by the sum of the terms, then multiply by each term.

scenes.animation: A class teacher pins test results on a board: 'Grade A 12, B 10, C 8, D 6, E 4 (40 students)'. A giant round pizza rolls in and Zippy holds a knife, confused about where to cut.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: The teacher wants a pie chart. How big should each slice be?

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Each slice's angle must be proportional to the number of students in that grade.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: A full circle is 360 degrees. So we split 360 in the ratio 12 is to 10 is to 8 is to 6 is to 4.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Divide by the HCF, 2, to get 6 is to 5 is to 4 is to 3 is to 2. The terms add to 20.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: 360 divided by 20 is 18 degrees for each part.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Grade A gets 6 times 18, which is 108 degrees. Grade B gets 90.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: C gets 72, D gets 54 and E gets 36 degrees.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Check: 108 plus 90 plus 72 plus 54 plus 36 is 360. The pie is complete.

scenes.animation: Construction animates step by step: a circle with radius AB; a protractor measures 108° anticlockwise from AB to draw AC; then 90° from AC to draw AD; then 72°, 54°, and the last 36° slice fills itself. The slices are coloured and labelled.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Now draw it. Draw a circle and one radius. Measure 108 degrees from it and draw the next radius.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: From that radius, measure 90 degrees, then 72, then 54. The last slice should come out as 36.

scenes.animation: A second pie: 'Entertainment 50%, Sports 25%, News 15%, Information 10%'. Steps: '50% of 360 = 180°', '25% = 90°', '15% = 54°', '10% = 36°'. An 'Exam Tip' sticker: 'Angles must total 360°'.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: What if the data is already in percentages?

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Even easier. 50 per cent of 360 is 180 degrees. 25 per cent is 90, 15 per cent is 54 and 10 per cent is 36.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Exam tip: always add your angles. If they don't make 360, recheck before drawing.

scenes.animation: Recap board with the finished, colourful pie chart. Points: '1. Slice angle ∝ quantity', '2. Angle = part ÷ total × 360°', '3. All angles add to 360°'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Recap.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: One: in a pie chart, each slice's angle is proportional to its quantity.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Two: the angle is the part divided by the total, times 360 degrees.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Three: all the angles must add up to 360.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: Now can we eat the pizza version?

scenes.animation: A road-laying crew of 20 workers finishes in 4 days. The foreman announces only 10 workers are available. Zippy calculates on a slate: '4 ÷ 2 = 2 days!'

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: Half the workers, so half the days. Two days!

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Fewer workers means more days, Zippy. Some quantities move in opposite directions.

scenes.animation: A table from Lucknow to Kanpur: 'Walk 5 km/h, 18 h', 'Bicycle 15 km/h, 6 h', 'Motorcycle 30 km/h, 3 h', 'Car 60 km/h, 1.5 h'. Arrows show '× 3' on speed and '× 1/3' on time. Every row's product glows '= 90 km'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Look at travelling from Lucknow to Kanpur. Walking at 5 kilometres per hour takes 18 hours. Cycling at 15 takes 6 hours.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Speed became 3 times, and time became one-third. They change by the same factor, but in opposite directions.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: In every row, speed times time is 90 kilometres. That's inverse proportion: x times y stays constant.

scenes.animation: Back to the road crew: '20 × 4 = 10 × y', '80 = 10y', 'y = 8 days'. Then pumps: '2 pumps × 18 h = 4 pumps × x', 'x = 36 ÷ 4 = 9 h'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: For the road, workers times days is constant. 20 times 4 is 80, so 10 workers need 8 days.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: 2 pumps fill a tank in 18 hours. With 4 pumps, 2 times 18 equals 4 times x, so x is 9 hours.

scenes.animation: A school kitchen store: 'Food for 80 students, 15 days'. Twenty more students arrive. Steps: '80 × 15 = 100 × x', '1200 = 100x', 'x = 12 days'. Then a contrast card: '5 workers move 4500 bricks → 18,000 bricks needs 20 workers (direct)'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Food for 80 students lasts 15 days. If 20 more join, 80 times 15 equals 100 times x. So x is 12 days.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: But not everything is inverse. If 5 workers move 4500 bricks a day, then 18,000 bricks need 20 workers. More bricks, more workers. That's direct.

scenes.animation: Ram and Shyam chop vegetables. 'Ram: 1 job in 1 h', 'Shyam: 1 job in 1.5 h → 2/3 job per hour'. Steps: 'together: 1 + 2/3 = 5/3 job per hour', 'time = 1 ÷ 5/3 = 3/5 h = 36 min'. An 'Exam Tip' sticker: 'Ask: does one go up when the other goes down?'.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: Ram cuts the vegetables in 1 hour, Shyam in 1.5 hours. Together, 2.5 hours?

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Together they must be faster! In one hour, Ram does 1 job and Shyam does two-thirds. That's five-thirds of a job each hour.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: So one job takes three-fifths of an hour, which is 36 minutes.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Exam tip: before using a rule, ask whether one quantity rises as the other falls. If yes, it's inverse.

scenes.animation: Recap board with the road crew and the Lucknow–Kanpur table. Points: '1. Inverse: one × n, the other × 1/n', '2. x × y = constant', '3. Direct: x ÷ y = constant'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Recap.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: One: in inverse proportion, when one quantity is multiplied by n, the other is divided by n.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Two: their product stays constant, like speed times time equals distance.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Three: in direct proportion, it's the quotient that stays constant.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: Eight days for the road. I'll bring snacks for the workers.
